title: Plugin picker and plugin options

controls.label: Profile config
controls.visible_when: always when the profile editor is open
controls.action: Hosts the preference screen that contains the Plugin category. U03 specifies this screen as C-U03-001.

controls.label: Plugin
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Category header above the plugin rows

controls.label: Plugin
controls.visible_when: always
controls.enabled_when: the profile subscription status is not Active
controls.action: Opens the plugin picker bottom sheet

controls.label: <selected plugin icon>
controls.visible_when: the plugin selected when the row initializes declares an icon. The preference icon is set to null, so the row has no image when that value is Disabled or an unknown id
controls.action: Shows the selected plugin app icon on the preference row

controls.label: <selected plugin label>
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Shows the selected plugin label, or Unknown plugin with the stored value

controls.label: Configure…
controls.visible_when: always
controls.enabled_when: the selected plugin entry exists and is not Disabled, and the profile subscription status is not Active
controls.action: Launches the plugin configuration activity, or the built-in options editor when none resolves
controls.navigates_to: Plugin configuration activity or plugin options editor

controls.label: <plugin options string>
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Shows the options of the selected plugin, without the plugin id. A plugin with no stored options shows its default config here

controls.label: Plugin picker
controls.visible_when: the Plugin row is tapped
controls.action: Shows the selectable plugins in a bottom sheet with vertical 8dp padding

controls.label: Plugin list
controls.visible_when: always while the picker is open
controls.action: Lists Disabled and every installed native plugin

controls.label: Disabled
controls.visible_when: always, first in discovery order
controls.action: Selects no plugin and closes the sheet

controls.label: <plugin label>
controls.visible_when: one row per exported content provider that answers ACTION_NATIVE_PLUGIN
controls.action: Selects that plugin and closes the sheet

controls.label: <plugin icon>
controls.visible_when: always; the ImageView is inflated for every row and its drawable is null when the plugin declares no icon
controls.action: Shows the 52dp plugin icon

controls.label: <plugin label>
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Shows the plugin label in bold when the row is the selected plugin

controls.label: <plugin id>
controls.visible_when: the plugin id is non-empty and differs from the label
controls.action: Shows the plugin id in bold when the row is the selected plugin

controls.label: Auto Connect unlock warning
controls.visible_when: the plugin is not direct-boot aware, Auto Connect is on, and the API level is 24 or higher
controls.action: Shows the amber lock-open icon and the tooltip This plugin might not work with Auto Connect

controls.label: Configure…
controls.visible_when: Configure… is tapped and no configuration activity resolves, or the activity returns RESULT_FALLBACK
controls.action: Edits the SIP003 options string in the built-in editor

controls.label: Plugin options
controls.visible_when: the options dialog is open
controls.action: Accepts the options string in a monospace EditText prefilled with the options of the selected plugin, or its default config when none is stored

controls.label: OK
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Parses the text and stores it as the options of the selected plugin

controls.label: Cancel
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Closes the dialog without changing the stored options

controls.visible_when: the selected plugin resolves an ACTION_HELP activity
controls.action: Launches plugin help with the current options text. The stock AlertDialog also dismisses the options editor on this click and discards the typed edit

controls.visible_when: the help activity returns RESULT_OK
controls.action: Shows the message from EXTRA_HELP_MESSAGE. A RESULT_OK without the extra opens the dialog with an empty message

controls.label: Plugin configuration activity
controls.visible_when: the selected plugin declares an ACTION_CONFIGURE activity
controls.action: Lets the plugin edit its options and returns RESULT_OK, RESULT_FALLBACK, or RESULT_CANCELED

controls.label: App info
controls.visible_when: an installed plugin row is long-pressed and the system settings activity resolves
controls.action: Opens the Android application details settings of the plugin package

controls.label: Warning: This plugin does not seem to come from a known trusted source.
controls.visible_when: the newly selected plugin is not signed by a trusted key
controls.action: Warns for the long snackbar duration

controls.label: <options parse error message>
controls.visible_when: the options text fails to parse
controls.action: Shows the exception message and refuses the change

controls.label: Conflicting plugins found from: <packages>
controls.visible_when: two providers declare the same plugin id, or a plugin declares an alias that another plugin already uses
controls.action: Builds the message from the providers whose id equals the later plugin's id, so a duplicate id names both packages while an alias conflict names only the later plugin's package. The list build then throws IllegalStateException

controls.label: Plugin: <id>
controls.visible_when: the profile's plugin id is non-empty
controls.action: Appends the plugin id line to the profile row details

controls.label: Failed to connect the remote server: <message>
controls.visible_when: the service stops with a failure message, such as Unknown plugin <id> or UDP fallback cannot have plugins
controls.action: Reports the start failure and leaves the service stopped

controls.label: <settings icon>
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Shows the static settings icon that the Configure… row declares

rules.statement: The Plugin row summary shows the selected plugin label, or Unknown plugin with the stored value.

examples.given: obfs-local is installed and selected
examples.when: the profile editor draws the Plugin row
examples.then: the summary reads the label the plugin app declares

examples.given: the stored plugin id is kcptun and no package declares it
examples.when: the profile editor draws the Plugin row
examples.then: the summary reads Unknown plugin kcptun

rules.statement: When the row initializes, the Plugin row icon is the icon of the selected plugin, and empty when the value is Disabled or an unknown id. A later picker selection does not refresh it (R-UH-09).

examples.given: obfs-local is selected when the row initializes
examples.then: the row shows the obfs-local app icon

examples.given: Disabled is the value when the row initializes
examples.then: the row shows no icon

rules.statement: Tapping the Plugin row opens a bottom sheet that lists Disabled and every exported native plugin provider.

examples.given: two native plugin packages are installed
examples.when: the user taps the Plugin row
examples.then: the sheet lists Disabled and both plugins

examples.given: no package exports a native plugin provider
examples.when: the user taps the Plugin row
examples.then: the sheet lists only Disabled

rules.statement: When the current value resolves, the picker moves it to the first row, skips it at its discovery position, and draws its label bold. The id line is shown and bold only when the id is non-empty and differs from the label.

examples.given: obfs-local is the current plugin and sits at index 1
examples.then: row 0 shows obfs-local in bold, obfs-local appears only once, and the other rows follow in discovery order

examples.given: the current value is Disabled
examples.then: row 0 shows Disabled in bold with no id line, and the installed plugins follow in discovery order

examples.given: the stored plugin id is unknown
examples.then: no row is moved and discovery order is kept

rules.statement: A plugin row shows its id below the label only when the id is non-empty and differs from the label.

examples.given: a plugin whose label differs from its id
examples.then: the second line shows the id

examples.given: the Disabled row with an empty id
examples.then: the second line is hidden

rules.statement: The unlock warning icon shows when the plugin is not direct-boot aware, Auto Connect is on, and the API level is 24 or higher.

examples.given: Auto Connect is on and the plugin provider is not directBootAware
examples.then: the amber lock-open icon is visible

examples.given: Auto Connect is off
examples.then: the icon is gone

examples.given: Auto Connect is on and the device runs API 23
examples.then: the icon never shows because directBootAware is true below API 24

rules.statement: Tapping a row closes the sheet and reports the plugin id only when it differs from the current value.

examples.given: obfs-local is current
examples.then: the sheet closes and the editor receives v2ray-plugin

examples.given: obfs-local is current
examples.when: the user taps the first row that shows obfs-local
examples.then: the sheet closes and no result is sent

rules.statement: Long-pressing an installed plugin row opens the system application details screen of that plugin package.

examples.given: an installed plugin row
examples.then: App info for the plugin package opens

examples.given: no activity handles application details
examples.then: the long press returns false and nothing opens

rules.statement: Selecting a plugin writes the new plugin string, marks the profile dirty, updates the Configure… row, and refreshes the summary. The row icon is not refreshed on this path; it keeps the icon set when the editor opened.

examples.given: obfs-local is selected
examples.then: the draft plugin string changes, the profile is dirty, the summary shows the v2ray-plugin label, and the row still shows the obfs-local icon until the editor is reopened

examples.given: a known plugin is selected
examples.then: the summary reads Disabled, Configure… is disabled, and the row still shows the previous plugin icon until the editor is reopened

rules.statement: Picking Disabled disables Configure…, and picking a known plugin enables it.

examples.given: a known plugin is selected
examples.then: Configure… becomes disabled

examples.given: Disabled is selected
examples.then: Configure… becomes enabled

examples.given: the stored plugin id is unknown, so Configure… is disabled
examples.then: Configure… stays disabled

rules.statement: Configure… stays disabled when the stored plugin id resolves to no installed plugin.

examples.given: the stored id is kcptun and no package provides it
examples.then: Configure… is disabled

examples.given: the stored id is obfs-local and the installed provider declares it
examples.then: Configure… is enabled

rules.statement: Selecting a plugin that is not signed by a trusted source shows the warning snackbar.

examples.given: an untrusted plugin app is installed
examples.then: the warning snackbar appears

examples.given: Disabled or a trusted plugin
examples.then: no warning appears

rules.statement: Tapping Configure… starts the plugin ACTION_CONFIGURE activity, or the built-in editor when none resolves.

examples.given: the plugin resolves ACTION_CONFIGURE
examples.then: the plugin activity opens with the options extra

examples.given: no activity resolves
examples.then: the built-in options editor opens

rules.statement: RESULT_OK from the configuration activity replaces the stored options for the selected plugin, and clears them when the result carries no EXTRA_OPTIONS.

examples.given: the plugin activity returns RESULT_OK with obfs=http
examples.then: the stored options become obfs=http

examples.given: the plugin activity returns RESULT_OK with a control character
examples.then: the change is refused and the error snackbar shows

examples.given: the plugin activity returns RESULT_OK with no EXTRA_OPTIONS, or with a null data Intent
examples.then: the stored options are cleared and the Configure… summary is empty

rules.statement: RESULT_FALLBACK from the configuration activity opens the built-in options editor.

examples.given: the plugin activity returns RESULT_FALLBACK
examples.then: the built-in editor opens with the stored options

examples.given: the plugin activity returns RESULT_CANCELED
examples.then: the built-in editor does not open and the stored options stay

rules.statement: Options that contain a control character are rejected and the previous options are kept.

examples.given: the field holds obfs=tls
examples.when: the user enters a newline and taps OK
examples.then: a snackbar reads No control characters allowed. and the old options stay

examples.given: the field holds obfs=tls
examples.then: the options are stored

rules.statement: The built-in editor shows the options of the selected plugin in a monospace field: the stored options, or the default config when none is stored.

examples.given: obfs-local is selected with obfs=tls
examples.then: the monospace field shows obfs=tls

examples.given: obfs-local is selected with no stored options, and it declares default_config obfs=tls
examples.then: the monospace field shows obfs=tls

rules.statement: The ? button appears only when the plugin resolves ACTION_HELP, and it passes the current text.

examples.given: the plugin resolves ACTION_HELP
examples.then: a ? neutral button is shown

examples.given: no help activity resolves
examples.then: no ? button is shown

rules.statement: A help callback result shows its message in an alert dialog titled ?. A RESULT_OK without EXTRA_HELP_MESSAGE still opens the alert, with an empty message.

examples.given: the help activity returns RESULT_OK with a message
examples.then: an alert titled ? shows the message

examples.given: the help activity returns RESULT_CANCELED
examples.then: no alert is shown

examples.given: the help activity returns RESULT_OK without EXTRA_HELP_MESSAGE
examples.then: an alert titled ? opens with an empty message

rules.statement: The plugin id and options are saved into the profile and written to ss URLs and JSON.

examples.given: plugin v2ray-plugin with mode=websocket
examples.then: the URL carries the plugin query and the JSON carries plugin and plugin_opts

examples.given: no plugin is selected
examples.then: no plugin query or JSON field is written

rules.statement: A newly selected plugin without stored options takes the plugin's default config as its options.

examples.given: a plugin declares default_config obfs=tls and has no stored options
examples.then: the Configure… text shows obfs=tls

examples.given: a plugin declares no default config
examples.then: the Configure… text is empty

rules.statement: Opening a profile owned by an active subscription disables the Plugin and Configure… rows. A later package install or removal re-runs initPlugins and can enable Configure… again from the plugin value while the Plugin row stays disabled.

examples.given: an active subscription profile with a known plugin stored
examples.then: the Plugin and Configure… rows are disabled

examples.given: a manual profile whose stored plugin resolves to an installed plugin
examples.then: both rows are enabled

examples.given: a manual profile whose plugin value is Disabled
examples.then: the Plugin row is enabled and the Configure… row is disabled

rules.statement: Plugin discovery is cached and rebuilt after any package install or removal.

examples.given: a plugin package is installed while the editor is open
examples.then: the plugin list is rebuilt and the row refreshes

examples.given: nothing changed
examples.then: the cached list is returned

rules.statement: Two providers declaring the same plugin id produce a conflict toast that names both packages, and the list build throws IllegalStateException. For an alias collision the toast names only the later plugin's package.

examples.given: two packages declare plugin id obfs-local
examples.then: a toast names both packages and IllegalStateException is thrown

examples.given: a plugin declares the alias obfs-local while another plugin uses obfs-local as its id
examples.then: the toast names only the later plugin's package and IllegalStateException is thrown

examples.given: two installed providers declare different plugin ids
examples.then: both plugins are listed and no conflict toast appears

rules.statement: Starting with a plugin id that has no provider fails with Unknown plugin and stops the service.

examples.given: the profile plugin is kcptun and no provider declares it
examples.then: a snackbar reads Failed to connect the remote server: Unknown plugin kcptun

examples.given: the plugin id is empty
examples.then: no plugin loads and the tunnel runs directly

rules.statement: A profile with a plugin runs TCP only, and a UDP fallback profile with a plugin is refused.

examples.given: a profile with a plugin and no UDP fallback
examples.then: the mode is tcp_only

examples.given: a UDP fallback profile with a plugin
examples.then: the start fails with UDP fallback cannot have plugins

rules.statement: The profile list row adds a Plugin line with the plugin id when the profile has one.

examples.given: a profile with plugin obfs-local
examples.then: the details read Plugin: obfs-local

examples.given: a profile without a plugin
examples.then: no plugin line appears

rules.statement: Selecting a plugin configured under an alias keeps those options and selects that alias id.

examples.given: options are stored under alias simple-obfs
examples.when: the user picks the plugin whose id is obfs-local
examples.then: the alias entry is selected and its options stay

examples.given: options are stored under the plugin id obfs-local
examples.when: the user picks the plugin whose id is obfs-local
examples.then: the obfs-local entry is selected and its options stay

rules.statement: Each plugin keeps its own options entry while another plugin is selected.

examples.given: obfs-local has obfs=tls and v2ray-plugin has mode=websocket
examples.then: each Configure… summary shows its own options

examples.given: obfs-local has obfs=tls stored, and v2ray-plugin has no stored entry and no default config
examples.when: the user switches from obfs-local to v2ray-plugin and back
examples.then: v2ray-plugin shows an empty summary, and obfs-local still shows obfs=tls

rules.statement: Options use semicolons, equals signs, and backslash escapes; bare words become flag keys.

examples.given: the text obfs=http;obfs-host=x
examples.then: obfs=http and obfs-host=x are stored

examples.given: the text a;b
examples.when: it is parsed as options without an id
examples.then: a and b become flag keys with null values

examples.given: the text mode=websocket;tls;host=example.com
examples.when: it is parsed, stored, and serialized again
examples.then: the entries come out in hash-map order, for example mode=websocket;host=example.com;tls

exceptions: The plugin package is removed while the sheet is open: the next package broadcast rebuilds the list. A row bound from the old list then sends an id that the new lookup does not contain, and the result listener throws NoSuchElementException; without a tap the row refreshes to Unknown plugin.
Two providers declare the same plugin id or alias: a toast names the packages that share the later plugin's id, and PluginList throws IllegalStateException.
The system has no activity for application details: the long press returns false and the sheet stays open.

notes: All 12 listed files exist. mobile/src/main/res/values/strings.xml does not exist: the mobile module has no strings of its own, so every label comes from core/src/main/res/values/strings.xml lines 152-159. The Plugin category is declared in mobile/src/main/res/xml/pref_profile.xml lines 72-95, which the unit map assigns to U03; this spec covers its Plugin and Configure… rows and leaves the UDP Fallback row to U03. U03 also specifies the rows and the editor as C-U03-019, C-U03-020 and C-U03-041 to C-U03-049; where the two units differ, the fields here are the source-verified ones, including the subscription lock on Configure… and its re-enable after a package change. C-U08-001 is the U03 profile editor screen, included here as the root of the plugin controls; C-U08-027 is the plugin line inside the U02 profile row. The stock dialog buttons and the EditText carry framework ids (android.R.id.button1, button2, button3, edit), not custom layout ids. The ? button is the neutral button. A click on any stock AlertDialog button dismisses the dialog, so the ? click closes the options editor and discards the typed text before the help activity starts. The help alert opens on RESULT_OK alone and is empty when EXTRA_HELP_MESSAGE is absent. The picker bottom sheet has no title, so C-U08-008 is named for the screen it represents; C-U08-016 takes its title from the Configure… preference; the help button and help dialog use the literal string ? and are not resources. The Plugin row icon is set by PluginPreference.init() and by its internal change listener only, so a picker selection leaves the previous drawable until the editor is reopened; the Configure… row carries a static settings icon (C-U08-029). The options are a HashMap, so the stored and exported string order can differ from the typed order; the live dialog, the Configure… summary and an immediate reopen keep the typed text because EditTextPreferenceDialogFragmentCompat sets the preference text to the field value. The conflict message is a Toast; the schema has no toast type, so it is recorded as a snackbar. It lists the providers whose id equals the later plugin's id, so a duplicate id names both packages and an alias conflict names one. Android discovers plugins as external APKs through content providers, so trust, app-info, package changes, configuration activities and help activities depend on Android package surfaces. HarmonyOS has no external plugins: it offers two built-in in-process plugins (native/sslocal-ffi/src/plugin.rs lines 129-131) behind a plain Select of none, obfs-local and v2ray-plugin plus the imported name (entry/src/main/ets/pages/ProfileEdit.ets lines 43 and 104-108), and a free-text options field with fixed placeholder hints (lines 310-326). Plugin and options persist in model/Profile.ets and model/ProfilesFile.ets and are written to ss URLs (Profile.ets lines 350-352), the SOCKS config (lines 499-501) and the tun config (lines 577-579). Unknown names fail at start in the core with SSLOCAL_ERR_BAD_CONFIG (native/sslocal-ffi/src/lib.rs line 201). The legacy kcptun command-line line parser (PluginConfiguration.kt lines 31-50) is Android compatibility only and has no HarmonyOS counterpart. The HarmonyOS select and options field are disabled for subscription-owned profiles (ProfileEdit.ets lines 111, 314 and 324), which matches the Android lock.
